note: Words for the opening cards (scripts/ui/intro.gd), the counter guide (scripts/ui/guide.gd) and the first-night training (scripts/ui/coach.gd). First written by the assistant on 2026-11-15 after the student's eleven notes. Version 2 (2026-11-16) is the guide for the counter-first screen: four pages, one each for the window, the left wall, the right wall and the desk. Version 3 (2026-11-17) adds the contact list and the paid calm-patch to the guide and the training: one tip at a time on the first night, each pointing at one thing. A tip has an id, the phases of a visit it belongs to (wait, exam, slip; a comma-separated list), the event that completes it (until; "next" for a tip that is only read), the area it points at (main.gd: _coach_focus) and its text, which must fit four lines of the box. Every tip also has NEXT, and SKIP ALL [K] ends the training; nothing in it is a step the player has to take. Version 4 (2026-11-17) tells the student's story in six cards: fired from Kessler, the debt Kessler sold to Harrow Credit, the Lanterns' back-street clinic and its contacts, Harrow's line, the drift (illegal street chrome) and the counter. The Lanterns card's picture is a list with two made-up entries: their aliases and codes are not in data/contacts.json, and each pair of clues fits nobody in the cast (tests/run_tests.gd checks it), so the picture cannot be taken for a real night's list. On 2026-11-19, when five characters joined the cast, KESTREL's second clue became 'Here to fix a part.', since 'Fee 400 or more.' fitted Lux Ferreira (19, fee 500). Version 5 (2026-11-18) redraws the pictures for that story after the student noticed the opening still showed the old one: FIRED is a strip of three panels (the badge refused on Kessler's floor 88, which is TOP_FLOOR in intro.gd; the lift down between two guards; outside in the rain, still holding Kessler's spec binder, tabbed EYES, HANDS, PORTS and VOICE); THE DEBT is Kessler's staff debt file stamped SOLD TO HARROW, with Harrow's lease slid over it; THE LANTERNS tags the matched patient CONTACT and the parcel PACKAGE; THE DRIFT is a crate of military surplus with its serials filed off and, through the glass, a visitor whose eye implant glitches before they crack the pane. The binder is why the reference sheet is drawn per implant model (data/parts.json): Kessler's spec pages for the parts this patient carries. No picture shows a member of tonight's cast. The word "chrome" left the rule text; it says "implant". Version 6 (2026-11-18) follows rules version 8, where right and wrong are told only at closing: the guide says the card holds the player's own notes and that bounties and bills come in at closing. Version 7 (2026-11-20, after the student's play) follows rules version 10: the guide's PATIENCE and TALK items and the training's talk tip say that the second PRESS breaks a patient and takes every lamp left, the steady walking out and the drifting lunging. Nobody has playtested any of it. {per_hour}, {hours}, {total}, {threshold}, {repair_cost}, {pay}, {code_cost}, {calm_cost}, {calm_gain}, {ask_cost}, {press_cost}, {per_night} and {limit} are filled in from rules.json and sheet.json; a rule set with no repair_cost leaves the "mend" item out. The pictures and the positions of the guide's numbers are drawn in code; only the words live here, so tools/art/measure_text.py can check that they fit.

cards.title: FIRED
cards.text: Twelve years at Kessler, up in the towers, fitting implants to people who could pay. Then one night your badge stopped opening doors, and security walked you all the way down. You kept one thing: Kessler's spec binder.

cards.title: THE DEBT
cards.text: Kessler sold everything you owed to Harrow Credit: the flat, the licence, the loan on your own two hands. Now the chair, the tools and the hands are on lease.

labels.head: HARROW CREDIT
labels.foot: Metered hourly. Shortfall recovered in kind.

cards.title: THE LANTERNS
cards.text: One counter still takes you: a back-street clinic run by the Lanterns, a street gang. Some patients are really their contacts, smuggling military implants. Tonight's list says who to look for. Say the code to the one who fits, and the gang pays {pay} for the package.

cards.title: THE LINE
cards.text: Harrow's meter reads your till every hour, and every hour it wants {per_hour} more. Fees and packages both count. End the night under the line and Harrow makes the cut: the lease is called in, hands first.

cards.title: THE DRIFT
cards.text: Street implants are illegal: cheap, unlicensed, sometimes torn out of a soldier. Some who wear them start to drift, and a drifting one can turn on you without warning. Most are only tired, scared or angry.

cards.title: BEFORE THE CUT
cards.text: So you check them first, against the binder. TREAT the steady and the fee is yours. Call TRAUMA TEAM on the drifting. If one turns on you, drop the SHUTTER before the glass gives.

items.text: THE PATIENT. Click eyes, hands or port for a closer look. Looking is free.
PATIENCE. Tools, questions, PRESS and wrong codes cost lamps. When the last one goes out they leave: no fee, no fine.
GLASS. What the pane can still take tonight. Every blow that lands leaves less time at the next attack.
REFERENCE SHEET [R]. Kessler's spec pages for this patient's models: what steady looks like, and what is merely odd. Click it to take it down. It never decides for you.
CONTACT LIST [L]. Tonight's contacts: an alias, two clues and a code each. SAY the code to the one visitor who fits both clues: a package, +{pay}. Anyone else: -{code_cost} patience.
TILL and HOUR. One patient is one hour. The meter reads the till each hour: stay over the line. Treated or handed over, a patient's fee comes in; the bills come at closing, before the last reading.
HALL CAMERA [C]. Who is next. Click it, then the big screen, to buzz them in. ENTER does it at once.

INTAKE CARD [N]. Your notes on the patient, written as you work; tick or cross a row yourself. {threshold} crosses: drifting, by the house rule. The call stays yours. Whether it was right, you learn at closing.
COUNTER GUIDE [H]. These pages. On your first night a TRAINING box points at one thing at a time; SKIP ALL [K] ends it.
TREAT. Pick up the stamp and stamp the card. For the steady.
TRAUMA TEAM. Press twice and they take the patient away. For the drifting.
SHUTTER [SPACE]. If a patient turns on you, drop it before the red bar runs out.
GLASS [G]. Between patients, {repair_cost} credits put one layer back in the pane.

guide.title: THE DESK

items.text: TOOLS. Penlight, grip bar, port check. Each costs patience and gives one reading.
YOUR OWN WORDS. T types a line. With the patient AI running, hold TAB to speak it.

TALK. ASK a question. CALM gives patience back, but each calm-patch costs {calm_cost} credits. PRESS pushes them hard. A second PRESS breaks them and takes every lamp: the steady walk out, the drifting lunge.

guide.closing: Nothing is required. Decide whenever you like. H opens this guide again.

training.text: TONIGHT'S CONTACTS hang on the left wall: the people the crew is waiting on. Click the list, or press L.
Each contact: an alias, two clues, a code. The one visitor who fits BOTH is theirs. The card has age, fee and request; a look shows the eyes.
The HALL CAMERA shows who is waiting. Click it, then the big screen, or press ENTER to buzz them in.
Their INTAKE CARD [N] hangs on the right wall: name, age, fee, request, and your notes as you work.
Card out, list out [L]: do both clues of one entry fit? Press SAY beside it. A wrong code costs {code_cost} patience.
Right code: a package, +{pay} in the till. Wrong: a blank look. Neither tells you anything about the patient.
Now the exam. The REFERENCE SHEET [R]: Kessler's specs for this patient's models, what steady looks like. It comes down where the list does.
PENLIGHT: move the light onto each eye. The readout says what each did; the sheet, what its model should.
GRIP: hold the mouse till the force gauge fills, then let go to say RELEASE. Steady lets go before the LIMIT mark.
PORT: a close look at the socket. Calm skin is fine. Dark threads spreading from it are not.
TALK: ASK costs {ask_cost}. PRESS costs {press_cost} and tests temper; a second PRESS takes every lamp. CALM gives {calm_gain} back for {calm_cost} credits.
Tick or cross each row of the card against the sheet. Your marks help you count: nothing scores them.
Steady? Pick up TREAT and stamp the card. {threshold} broken lines mean drifting: call TRAUMA TEAM, press twice.
From now on a drifting patient may turn on you mid-exam. A red bar: SHUTTER [SPACE], now. A shout with no red bar is only temper.
